We would like to offer a warm welcome to all the children who will be joining us in Reception for September 2026.

Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND)
The Governors and staff of St. Nicholas C.E. Infants’ School recognise that all children have a right to a broad, balanced, relevant and differentiated curriculum. We aim to create a happy, educationally exciting and positive environment in which all pupils can develop to their full potential and become confident, independent individuals.
Information and Guidance
Who should I contact to discuss the concerns or needs of my child?
St Nicholas CE Infants' School is committed to working in partnership with parents and will listen to any concerns parents may wish to raise. Please contact the school to arrange a meeting.
In addition, parents and carers can contact SENDIASS (who will be able to provide you with advice and support.
Use the link below or telephone 01865 810516 (term–time only).
Our Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator is Mrs Grace Challans. You can contact her via the school office on 01491 836408 or email senco@st-nicholas.co.uk.
The Oxfordshire County Council Local Offer for Children with SEN and disabilities

pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care (including extra-curricular after-school clubs)
Wraparound Care (including extra-curricular after-school clubs)
Early Bird Breakfast Club
Our breakfast club operates from 7.50am to 8.30am, Monday to Friday, and is offered exclusively to children of our school in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2.
The cost per child per day for the club is £5.00 if booked in advance. Short notice emergency slots may be available at a cost of £6.25 per child per day and must be booked online via the link below. If the booking system is full, please call the office to confirm if there is any space available.
Children are given breakfast (typically a selection of cereals, toast, fruit juice and milk) and will then have the opportunity to enjoy reading, games, puzzles and other activities. The club is run by school staff, and overseen by Miss King/Ms Ghezzi.
Please note that breakfast is served between 7.50am and 8.15am.
If you would like to make a booking, please follow the link: https://stnicholasceinfantsschool.kidsclubhq.co.uk/cust#/register
Breakfast Club terms and conditions
Puffins After School Club
Fees are £17.00 per session, booked in advance, and these run from 3.00pm - 5.30pm, Monday to Friday. Short notice emergency sessions may be available at a cost of £19.00 per child per day and must be booked online via the link below. If the booking system is full, please call the office to confirm if there is any space available.
Children will be given a snack (typically a selection of toast, bagels, fruit, veg, fruit juice and milk). They will have the opportunity to enjoy reading, games, crafts and a variety of other activities, both indoors and out. Puffins is run by school staff and a member of the school's Safeguarding Team is always on site.
To make a booking, please follow this link:
https://stnicholasceinfantsschool.kidsclubhq.co.uk/cust#/register
Puffins After School Club terms and conditions
Extra-Curricular After-School Clubs
We run a range of fun and engaging clubs to enhance our curriculum. These usually run from 15.00 - 16.00 on some days of the week.
Here are some examples of clubs we have run in the past:
Boogie Bugs Bright Sparks Science Computer Club Gymnastics Yoga Netball Club Football Club Fencing Italian Craft Club
Book Club Lacrosse Multi-skills
Clubs run before or after school and are offered for much of the academic year, usually for five weeks before and after every half-term break. Every full term parents/carers are informed which clubs are available and we encourage parents/carers to make the choice with their child.
Please note, not all clubs are available for all age ranges and some may have a small charge.

pageCache.text:
Nursery
ST NICHOLAS SCHOOL NURSERY
Mallards is a long-established Nursery Class led by an experienced, fully qualified teacher. Mrs Taylor has extensive teaching experience and a real passion for teaching in the early years. Our nursery is very much part of the wider school and the children join in with key events and celebrations throughout the year.
We have 42 places available with a maximum of 21 children in any single session.
Our morning sessions run from 8:30 to 11:30 and our afternoon sessions run from 12:00 to 15:00. Our lunch sessions run from 11:30am to 12:00pm.
For security management, drop-off times are 08:30 or 12:00 and pick-up times are 11:30 or 15:00.
We offer the Universal Entitlement of 15 funded hours and we also offer the Working Parent Entitlement (WPE) of 30 hours for those who qualify.
All sessions, and our lunch session, can be included in funded hours (if entitlement is sufficient) OR charged at our standard rates.
For additional sessions that are not covered by the Universal Entitlement or Working Parent Entitlement, charges are £19.50 per 3-hour session and £6.50 per hour for any additional hours. (With effect from September 2026 these charges will increase to £21.00 per 3-hour session and £7.00 per hour for additional hours.)
For children who attend five full days a week, this equates to 32.5 hours and therefore exceeds the 30 hours entitlement of funding. An additional charge would be payable and, at current prices, this would be £16.25 per week (from September 2026, this will increase to £17.50 per week)
For children who attend the maximum number of funded hours (where eligible for WPE), to avoid paying additional charges, pick-up would need to be at the end of a morning session on one of the days.
Parents are asked to provide a healthy packed lunch for their children who attend the lunch session. During the morning and afternoon sessions, a healthy snack of fruit or vegetables is provided free of charge.
Please contact the school office on 01491 836408 or email office@st-nicholas.co.uk to request a registration form, or download one - see below. Our Nursery Admissions Policy can also be found below. This includes details of how nursery places are allocated when more applications are received than there are places available.

Please note that the process of applying for a place in our nursery class is separate to that of applying for a place in school for the Reception year.

pageCache.text:
Governors
Welcome from the Local Governing Body
Oxford Diocesan Schools Trust (ODST) delegates responsibility for the strategic management of its schools to each Local Governing Body.
We are committed to ensuring that St Nicholas provides everyone here, children and adults alike, with an environment where they can become the best they can be.
The level of dedication and commitment shown by the school leadership team, the teaching and support staff, and the children is amazing. We are privileged to be able to come into school and see first hand the brilliant learning and the happy atmosphere everyone works hard to provide.
As a governing body, we work together to ensure that our school is always focused on providing the best possible start in education for all of our children. As a Church of England school, we also ensure that our children can grow and learn within a school community based on distinctly Christian values that welcomes pupils and parents of all faiths and none.
We are responsible for ensuring the school constantly works towards its vision, for providing strategic direction and financial oversight, and supporting and challenging school leaders in equal measure to ensure a focus on continuing success.
There is more information about the role and membership of the Governing Body on these pages, but if you have questions please contact the clerk to the governors in the first instance, via email or by telephoning the school office.

If you wish to contact the Governors, please email: chair@st-nicholas.co.uk

pageCache.text:
Maths
At St Nicholas CE Infants' School, we strongly believe in making Maths purposeful and visual. The use of practical resources, real-life connections and models and images for children to 'hook' their understanding of concepts onto is vital for embedding a good basis for further mathematical learning and is a big feature of the curriculum. A mathematically rich environment is also key for supporting learning.
We believe it is important that children consolidate their understanding of number and calculation using a variety of models and images such as number lines, the part-whole model and tens frames, before moving onto compact written methods. This ensures children are more likely to grasp these concepts and methods later on due to their sound understanding of how each process 'works'.
In Nursery and Reception we use Development Matters to inform our teaching and assessment of Number as well as Shape, Space and Measure. Much of the learning takes place in the indoor and outdoor provision and in addition to this small group guided teaching addresses new concepts and helps the children develop and consolidate new skills.
In Key Stage 1 we use the White Rose Maths Hub Scheme of Learning which can be found below. This works on the belief that all children, when introduced to a new concept, should have the opportunity to build competency by taking the Concrete - Pictorial - Abstract approach:
Concrete - children should have the opportunity to use concrete objects and manipulatives to help them understand what they are doing.
Pictorial - alongside this children should use pictorial representations. These representations can then be used to help reason and solve problems.
Abstract - both concrete and pictorial representations should support children's understanding of abstract methods.
Mastering Number is a daily programme we use from Reception to Year 2 that sits alongside our White Rose Maths Curriculum. It helps children develop a deep, secure understanding of number. Through short, engaging sessions, pupils build strong number sense, grow in confidence and become fluent with early calculation.
Children explore numbers in lots of practical ways, using visual models and manipulatives to spot patterns, make connections and explain their thinking. This steady, structured approach means they develop the strong foundations they need for later success in maths.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music | St Nicholas CofE Infants' School
pageCache.text:
Music
Music is an important part of life at St Nicholas. We want every child to enjoy making music, feel proud of their progress, and grow in confidence as they explore their creativity. Our music curriculum helps children develop a love of music and the skills to express themselves as musicians, whether they’re singing, playing, composing or listening.
We follow the Creative Music scheme by Charanga, which is fully in line with the National Curriculum and EYFS guidance. The scheme offers a clear progression from year to year and introduces children to a wide range of musical styles and traditions. Lessons include active listening, performing and composing, helping children understand the language of music and the context behind what they hear and create.
Children are encouraged to use their singing voices, body percussion and instruments to explore sound and express musical ideas. They work individually, in pairs and in groups, with plenty of opportunities to collaborate, reflect and celebrate their achievements. Musical vocabulary is introduced in meaningful ways and children are supported to talk about music with growing confidence.
Throughout the year, children take part in performances and recordings, sharing their musical learning with peers and wider audiences. Music and singing are woven into school life, helping children build self-esteem, develop a sense of rhythm and pitch, and experience the joy of making music together.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reading | St Nicholas CofE Infants' School
pageCache.text:
Reading
At St Nicholas, we believe that reading is about much more than simply working out what the words say. We want every child to take pleasure in reading, to explore stories, build understanding and grow into confident, enthusiastic readers. Reading is a journey and families play a vital role in supporting it. A short daily reading session at home can make a real difference to a child’s progress, helping them develop fluency, deepen comprehension and nurture a lifelong love of books.
In school, phonics forms the foundation of our reading curriculum. Children learn to decode new words by linking letters to sounds, supported by Rhino Readers which is a carefully structured reading scheme matched to each child’s phonics level. These books are available to families via the Rhino Readers app, making home practice simple and effective. Alongside this, children take home an additional reading book and a library book to broaden their reading experience. As children move beyond phonics, we introduce ‘free reader’ texts to support growing independence and enjoyment.
Reading is woven into daily life at St Nicholas. Each year group has a set of core texts which are books chosen with care to ensure every child experiences the joy they offer. Every half term also features an ‘Author of the Term’, giving children the chance to explore a range of books by a single author and deepen their love of reading. We use shared reading to model fluency, expression and comprehension and guided reading to support children’s next steps in small groups. We also listen to children read individually, helping them build confidence and celebrate progress. Storytime is a treasured part of our day, where children encounter a wide range of texts, develop language and discover the joy of reading for pleasure.
Above all, we want children to see themselves readers who love books, are curious, capable and connected to the world through words.
Core texts play an important role in enriching our curriculum at St Nicholas. Each half term, every year group spends dedicated time with a carefully chosen book that is meant to be read aloud, lingered over and enjoyed together. These stories are selected for their richness, their language, their illustrations and their ability to spark curiosity. Core texts are shared with close attention to detail, drawing children into the illustrations and inviting their questions, predictions and reactions. By returning to the same story over time, pupils build familiarity, confidence and deeper understanding, while enjoying the rhythm, repetition and surprises that make these books so memorable.

pageCache.text:
Science
At St Nicholas, we want science to be meaningful, engaging and relevant to our children’s lives. We use Switched on Science to make sure all the content from the Primary Science National Curriculum is fully covered, giving every child their entitlement to a broad and balanced science education.
Units are carefully planned to build on what children have experienced in the EYFS, and to prepare them for what’s to come in Key Stage 2. Each year group explores six topics across the year, with regular opportunities for hands-on investigations, practical enquiry and thoughtful discussion. Children also develop their understanding of seasonal change throughout EYFS and KS1, helping them notice and describe patterns in the world around them.
Scientific enquiry is at the heart of our approach. Children learn to ask questions and explore ideas through five key types of enquiry:
Lessons are designed to be purposeful and accessible, with key vocabulary introduced and revisited to help children talk confidently about their learning. Where appropriate, ICT and practical equipment are used to support investigations and deepen understanding.
Science learning is recorded in whole-class floorbooks, where children’s questions, reflections, photos and group thinking are captured. These books celebrate the journey of discovery and give children a shared space to talk about what they’ve learned.
By the end of KS1, children at St Nicholas are curious, confident and ready to explore. They understand how science connects to their lives and the wider world, and they’re proud to share what they know and how they found it out.
